findings.claim: The plan touches two concepts and the decisions index but never says whether supersede appends a log.md line. The every-touched-concept-is-logged rule (.claude/rules/okf-bundle.md) is a gate in this repo, and the okf plugin logs every supersession as a lifecycle event. A supersede that leaves log.md alone gives the caller a change the okf check refuses. Either way works, but the scope must say which: kmctl appends a dated bullet naming both ids, or kmctl leaves that to the caller and says so in its output. Done-when should cover it.

Invariant I4 (.okf/manifesto.md) says kmctl uses only fields the OKF v0.2 spec defines (stale_after, verified, sources, status) and adds no extension fields. The plan's core output is decision_status, which is not a spec field (okf_validate.py knows only status). The repo's own records and okf-bundle.md use decision_status, so the conflict is in the contract, not the code: the test written for I4 would catch this command. The operator needs to say decision_status is a bundle convention kmctl may write, by rewording I4 or accepting the risk in the plan, before it is built.
